title: Draft: Qt: Adjust disclosure triangle and QTreeView indent.
description:
Make the proto tree UI disclosure triangle scale up or down to match the text
size.  Also scale the indent for child nodes within the tree.

The result is much more appealing at large text sizes and on HiDPI screens.

Note that Qt's default platform-specific tree-view widgets will no longer be
used after this change.

----

I don't usually poke around in the UI, and I have limited C++ experience and limited Qt experience, so please do let me know if I've taken the wrong approach here.  I read lots of Qt documentation to try to get it right. :smiley: 

----

Before-and-after screenshot on Linux:
![wireshark-proto-tree-widgets](/uploads/6f283dcab2d615588734db7850af599e/wireshark-proto-tree-widgets.png)

notes.body:
The default size is now bigger and thicker, this does not look good (at least on macOS).
Clicking the arrow does not always open/close the item.

> The default size is now bigger and thicker, this does not look good (at least on macOS).

I might have to make it platform-specific after all.  There is perhaps too much difference between the darker/heavier Linux tree widget and the lighter/thinner macOS tree widget for me to find any "middle ground".  Does that sound sensible?

> Clicking the arrow does not always open/close the item.

That is very confusing.  My change should only affect the widget's appearance, and should have no effect at all on its behavior.  The only thing I can think of is if I'm somehow drawing the widget in the wrong location so that the clicks miss the hit-box and "go somewhere else" and don't have the expected effect on the row of the tree view.  Ah... if I click in the rightmost half of the widget it works as expected, but clicking in the left half of it (particularly when the font size is small) acts as if I've clicked on the row outside the widget... Does that match what you experience there?  Interesting...  I might separate out the change to the indent and see if that is responsible for that behavior.

This is how it looks on macOS.
![PacketListOriginal](/uploads/38c734a91a987dbdc0a5675f93c96f55/PacketListOriginal.png)
![PacketListNew](/uploads/d5f469972239e205b4fc49c5b946e39a/PacketListNew.png)
Yeah, it seems I'm drawing my widget a bit further left from the macOS default widget, so clicks on its left side "miss" the widget.  Let me see if I can correct it.

I added an `p->fillRect(option->rect, QColor(255, 0, 0));` immediately prior to drawing the widget, and the widget is drawn completely inside the red rectangle.

I think the culprit here is Qt's `QMacStyle::subElementRect` (in `src/plugins/styles/mac/qmacstyle_mac.mm`) which does the following:


```
 261 static const int DisclosureOffset = 4;
```
...
```
4639 QRect QMacStyle::subElementRect(SubElement sr, const QStyleOption *opt,
4640                                 const QWidget *widget) const
4641 {           
```
...
```
4646     switch (sr) { 
```
...
```
4731     case SE_TreeViewDisclosureItem: {
4732         rect = opt->rect;
4733         // As previously returned by HIThemeGetButtonContentBounds
4734         rect.setLeft(rect.left() + 2 + DisclosureOffset);
4735         break;
4736     }
```

which trims 6 pixels from the left-hand side of the "hit box" for the disclosure widget.

There is a (nearly-)corresponding adjustment in the code which draws the widget:

```
2959 void QMacStyle::drawPrimitive(PrimitiveElement pe, const QStyleOption *opt, QPainter *p,
2960                               const QWidget *w) const
```
...
```
3280     case PE_IndicatorBranch: {
```
...
```
3291         QRect qtRect = opt->rect.adjusted(DisclosureOffset, 0, -DisclosureOffset, 0);
```

Let's see if I can override the bounds.
Did you have a look at resize the default arrow?

I tried but could not find a way to force the default arrow to resize.  Qt renders the default widgets at a certain size and caches the resulting pixmap, and then always uses that cached pixmap, seemingly without regard to the size it will be displayed.  Perhaps I am overlooking or misunderstanding something, but I could not get that default widget to resize.

This draft I think improves the overall appearance of the disclosure widgets.  It still looks a bit different from the regular macOS tree-view widget, but hopefully it is now of a size and line-weight that is more agreeable.

This draft also corrects the background for the disclosure widgets to be _more_ like it was before.  There is still one quirk that I can't figure out how to correct: On macOS, if you select a row in the proto tree and then move the focus elsewhere (e.g. by clicking on the already-selected packet in the packet list or by pressing *Tab* or *Shift+Tab*), the disclosure widget still has the blue "selected" background.  Interestingly, when you follow the same steps on Linux, the whole row retains the blue "selected" background... whereas on macOS the rest of the row (except the disclosure widget) changes.  I haven't yet figured out how to make that consistent again...

commits_data.title: Qt: Adjust proto tree disclosure widget size.
commits_data.message:
Qt: Adjust proto tree disclosure widget size.

Allow the tree-view disclosure widget to scale up or down according to the
tree-view's cell size.

Note that Qt's default platform-dependent tree-view "primitive
elements" will no longer be used after this change.

Make the proto tree indent proportional to the font size used.  This
improves the readability of the proto tree on HiDPI displays or at
large text sizes.

I've tested this on a Linux system and a Mac, but it is entirely
possible that usage on other platforms and displays might reveal the
need for further adjustments to the way the disclosure triangle is
drawn -- colors, pen, etc.
